summary: 24 weeks pregnant with MRI-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis: laparoscopic appendicectomy ranks above antibiotics-first; pregnancy lowers the antibiotics-first benefit.

inputs.hpi: 24 weeks pregnant (G2P1). 30 hours of periumbilical pain moving to the right flank, anorexia and nausea. No vaginal bleeding, fetal movements normal.

exam.abdomen: Gravid uterus at 24 weeks. Tender right flank and right iliac fossa with guarding; no generalised peritonism.

imaging.name: MRI abdomen
imaging.result: Dilated 9 mm appendix with periappendiceal inflammation, displaced superiorly; no appendicolith, no abscess, no free fluid.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis (uncomplicated) in pregnancy
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute uncomplicated appendicitis at 24 weeks' gestation, MRI-confirmed.

match: re:pregnant lowered the benefit of antibiotics-first

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S et al. World J Emerg Surg 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: CODA trial
guideline.citation: CODA Collaborative. N Engl J Med 2020;383:1907-1919.

rationale: Pregnant women were excluded from CODA and APPAC; WSES 2020 favours laparoscopic appendicectomy in pregnancy because failed non-operative treatment and perforation carry fetal risk.
